data.description:
## Observation
- `tests/scripts/reducer/test_cache_invalidated_on_file_deletion` (tests/scripts/reducer/test_reducer_cache.py:180) asserts the `.cache.json` mtime changes between the warm write and the post-deletion rewrite, using float `st_mtime`.
- In an ubuntu:26.04 container on a colima VM (Linux 6.8.0-117-generic, aarch64, overlayfs /tmp), 2026-11-09 PST, the test failed 16 of 30 runs with no sandbox and 18 of 30 under bwrap, each failure reading `assert 1794262869.4604867 != 1794262869.4604867`.
- It passes on GitHub's hosted runners (all pytest cells and run 42702801672's jobs passed).
- It is in the `reducer-processors` mutation shard, so a failure there fails that shard's clean baseline (`baseline-test: head/reducer-processors`), as seen when reproducing `unwasteful-increased-colt` locally.

## Hypotheses (unproven)
The two writes land within one kernel timestamp tick on hosts whose file timestamps are coarse (jiffy granularity), so the rewrite gets an identical mtime; or the second `reduce_ticket` call does not rewrite the cache on those hosts. Not yet distinguished.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The root cause is identified with a deterministic reproduction, and the test asserts cache recomputation in a way that does not depend on timestamp granularity.
data.title: test_cache_invalidated_on_file_deletion fails about half the time on a coarse-timestamp Linux host (equal mtime after rewrite)
